resources.string: Hides active VPN connection from selected apps — NetworkCapabilities, NetworkInfo, NetworkInterface, LinkProperties, /proc/net
VPN Hide did not receive any app list. No settings were removed. Tap Retry.
Couldn’t refresh every Android profile. Showing the previous complete app list; no settings were removed.
Couldn’t scan %1$s. Showing every app VPN Hide could read; settings for %1$s are kept.
Block every TCP and UDP connection to 127.0.0.1 and ::1 for this app. This is the default P behavior.
Block only the listed localhost ports. Leave End empty for a single port.
Enter at least one valid port or range from 1 to 65535.
LSPosed hides VPN signals exposed through Android Java APIs such as NetworkCapabilities, NetworkInfo, LinkProperties, and NetworkInterface.
The active native backend hides VPN signals visible through kernel or libc probes. VPN Hide writes one native selection to every installed native backend; only the active backend acts.
App-hiding observer mode. This app receives a sanitized package-manager view and cannot list, resolve, or query packages that VPN Hide marks as hidden.
Ports observer mode. The ports module makes localhost VPN/proxy daemon probes look like closed ports for this app. By default P blocks every localhost port; settings can limit it to selected ranges.
For Java, Native, and Ports, tap the settings icon next to the label to choose individual hooks or port ranges for this app. A * means this app has custom settings.

VPN Hide auto-detects packages that should be hidden from observers, including apps declaring a VPN service and optional name heuristics. Manual hidden-package choices live in Settings → Advanced hiding. System callers stay exempt so Android can keep installing and launching apps.
After Save, Java and kernel native backends (kmod/KPM) apply immediately. Zygisk native hooks and ports rules are picked up by a selected app after force-stop and reopen.
Zygisk hooks run inside the selected app process. Banking and payment apps may detect that when Native is enabled for them; leave Native off for those apps and rely on Java where possible.
Open VPN Hide in the main profile
Uninstall this copy of VPN Hide and use the copy installed in the main profile. It can manage apps from every profile.
VPN Hide needs root access to manage VPN hiding for selected apps. Grant it in your root manager (Magisk, KernelSU, APatch), then tap Check again.
Native limit reached: at most %1$d app UIDs can be selected. Disable Native for another app first.
Saved, but the Native backend can protect only %1$d of %2$d resolved app UIDs. The %3$d highest UIDs were left without Native protection.
Collect diagnostics into one file to send the developer. Choose what to include (logs, app list, kernel image).
VPN is off. This log will contain incomplete information and is little help for diagnosis. Turn the VPN on and re-check.
A VPN is up, but VPN Hide is not routed through it (split tunneling). This log will be incomplete. Add VPN Hide to the tunnel and re-check.
dmesg, logcat and raw kernel/network probes. Bigger file; usually what a bug report needs.
Reveals which apps you have installed. Off by default; enable only when the developer asks.
Attaches the active boot/kernel partitions. Large, takes ~a minute; produces a .zip. For boot/kernel bugs.
Off by default to keep logcat quiet and avoid the overhead. The capture tools in Debugging enable it automatically — turn this on only for continuous logs across every component.

Records unfiltered logs from all buffers (main/system/crash/events/radio) and saves a ZIP with device, backend, kernel, and config context. It can include sensitive app data and the agent-control token. Start recording, reproduce the bug, then stop.
Hook not installed on this kernel: %1$s — nothing covers this surface here.
VPN is active. Hiding is enabled for this app. Results below.
Enabled hiding for VPN Hide. Restart VPN Hide (force-stop and reopen) for native-level checks to take effect — no device reboot needed.
Network access is disabled for this app. ioctl checks (SIOCGIFFLAGS, SIOCGIFMTU, SIOCGIFCONF) cannot run without it. Enable in Settings → Apps → VPN Hide → Mobile data & Wi-Fi.

Detection surfaces the active backend doesn\'t cover — not a failure of the running module. VPN filesystem paths (e.g. /sys/class/net) are closed by turning on Experimental protection in Settings; other surfaces may need a kernel-level backend (kmod / KPM) where the device supports one.
VPN Hide could not collect the root state needed for this screen. Check your root manager if permission was interrupted, then tap Retry.
Refresh failed. Showing the previous dashboard data.
VPN Hide could not run a root command. If you denied or interrupted the root prompt, grant access in your root manager, then tap Retry.
Root access worked, but VPN Hide could not read part of its startup state (shown below). This is usually temporary — tap Retry.
Root access worked, but VPN Hide could not save its updated config (shown below). Tap Retry.
VPN Hide could not finish its root-side startup (shown below). Tap Retry.
VPN Hide could not collect the root state needed for this tab. Check your root manager if permission was interrupted, then tap Retry.
Installed, restart VPN Hide to activate
Installed, did not load — try the other GKI variant
Hiding is inactive without a VPN
VPN Hide just enabled hiding for itself. Restart VPN Hide (force-stop and reopen) to check hiding — no device reboot needed.
No active VPN. Turn it on, then tap Retry to run the hiding checks.

A VPN is active, but VPN Hide isn\'t routed through it. Add VPN Hide to your VPN\'s tunnel (don\'t exclude it with split tunneling), then tap Retry — otherwise there is nothing to hide from these checks.
The hiding checks couldn\'t run — root access may have been denied or a command failed. Tap Retry. This is usually transient.
Runtime events reported by active backends
No runtime statistics yet. Counters appear when a selected app calls an installed hook.
No counters yet from backends that support statistics.
Native counters are not available for Zygisk. Java and Apps counters are still reported by LSPosed.
KPM has more counters than its control channel can return in one snapshot. Partial native totals are hidden; Java and Apps counters are still reported by LSPosed.
VPN Hide could not collect the root state needed for this tab. Check your root manager if permission was interrupted, then tap Retry.
Refresh failed. Showing the previous statistics data.
Cumulative since boot. Tap an app for the full per-hook breakdown.
See exactly which VPN checks an app runs:
Switch to the app you want to test and use it for a bit.
Every VPN check it makes shows up in the list below.
Switch to the app you are testing and use it — probes show up below as they happen.
What the tested app probed since this session started. Tap for the per-hook breakdown.
Waiting for probes… switch to the app you are testing and use it.
Session stopped — these results stay until you start a new capture or clear them.
No probes were captured this session.
An app reads the routing table (/proc/net/route or netlink). A VPN installs a catch-all default route through its tunnel interface — its presence gives the VPN away.
An app enumerates network interfaces and their addresses (getifaddrs / netlink). A VPN appears as an extra tunNN interface with an address that doesn\'t match Wi-Fi or cellular.
An app queries interfaces directly via ioctl (SIOCGIFCONF / SIOCGIFFLAGS). The VPN tunnel interface shows up in the list or reports as up.
An app binds a socket by interface name or index (SO_BINDTODEVICE / SO_BINDTOIFINDEX). Whether the bind succeeds can reveal a hidden VPN interface or route traffic through it.
An app reads policy routing rules (RTM_GETRULE). A VPN adds rules that steer traffic into the tunnel, which betray its presence.
An app queries NetworkCapabilities. An active VPN sets the VPN transport flag — a direct signal that a VPN is up.
An app reads LinkProperties. A VPN exposes its tunNN interface name, VPN routes and DNS servers.
An app checks NetworkInfo (legacy API). An active VPN reports type VPN instead of mobile or Wi-Fi.
An app resolves the active Network handle. A VPN returns its own virtual network instead of the physical one.
An app lists all networks or subscribes to network callbacks via ConnectivityService. The VPN network shows up in the list or through callbacks.
An app lists installed packages or queries VpnService components. The presence of known VPN apps reveals VPN use.
\"%1$s\" in the kernel version is the GKI Kernel Module Interface tag — it identifies the kernel\'s binary interface to modules, not your Android OS release.
Kernel module is recommended. Your kernel\'s GKI branch isn\'t identifiable from uname -r, so try %1$s first; if it doesn\'t load into the kernel after reboot, install %2$s instead.
Kernel module is not supported for your device. Install %1$s.
Banking and payment apps may detect Zygisk hooks when Native is enabled for them. Leave Native off for those apps and rely on LSPosed (Java-level) hiding.
KPM is recommended for your kernel — a single universal module that hides at the kernel level, invisible to anti-tamper. Download %1$s.

KPM is recommended for your kernel — kernel-level hiding, invisible to anti-tamper. It needs the KPatch-Next-Module installed first. If you\'d rather not install that, use vpnhide-zygisk.zip instead. KPM artifact: %1$s.

The kernel module is the stable, most-tested choice. KPM is an alternative — one universal module, no GKI variant to match — useful if the kernel module won\'t load into your kernel (wrong variant, or the kernel enforces module signatures).
Your kernel supports the stealthier KPM, but only Zygisk is installed. Zygisk is detectable by banking/payment apps; KPM hides at the kernel level. Consider installing %1$s.
Questions, bug reports, or feedback? Reach the author here.
Chat with the community and the author
VPN Hide is free, has no ads and sends nothing anywhere. There will be no paid features — donating unlocks nothing. If the app turned out useful, you can chip in for its development.
VPN Hide is free and has no ads. If it is useful to you, you can support its development.
A configuration from a version before 1.0 was found on this device: %1$d apps. Your current setup already has apps configured, so it was not imported automatically.
Found %1$d apps: Java %2$d, Native %3$d, Apps %4$d, Ports %5$d, hidden %6$d.
%1$d app-hiding entries were saved as UIDs that no longer match an installed app and will be skipped.

Merge keeps everything configured now and adds the old roles on top. Replace drops the current app list and uses the old one instead; auto-hide settings and VPN Hide\'s own entry are kept either way. Delete removes the old files without reading them — pick it if you have already set everything up again and just want them off the device. All three delete the files; this cannot be undone.
The old files were deleted. Nothing was imported.
Nothing left to import — the old files are already gone.
Import failed (%1$s). Root access may have been denied.
Delete all config, state and target files VPN Hide left on the device
This permanently deletes every config, state, statistics and target file VPN Hide and its modules wrote outside their module folders. This cannot be undone.

Do this only after you have: removed all VPN Hide modules in your root manager, disabled the VPN Hide LSPosed module, and rebooted. Module folders, the app itself and runtime state are not touched here — they go away with the steps above.
Not ready yet — VPN Hide is still active. Remove these and reboot first:
Kernel hook is still loaded — reboot needed
Done. All leftover files were removed. You can now uninstall VPN Hide.
Could not remove the files. Make sure root access is granted and try again.

Your kernel supports the kernel module — it hooks in kernel space and is invisible to anti-tamper checks. Zygisk works too, but banking and payment apps may detect its hooks when Native is enabled for them. Install %1$s and uninstall the Zygisk module for cleaner coverage.

The kernel module (.ko) and the KPM are both installed. They hook the same kernel functions, and having both active can hard-freeze the device. Keep only one — uninstall either the kernel module or the KPM.
The kernel module (.ko) and the KPM are both installed. The KPM stood down at boot to avoid a freeze, so it isn\'t doing anything. Keep only one — uninstall the KPM (or the kernel module).
The KPM is installed but inactive: APatch/FolkPatch could not load it with the trusted su token. Save your SuperKey in Settings → Security, then reboot to activate native hiding.
The %1$s module is installed but not active yet — reboot the device to activate it.
The %1$s module installation is corrupted: its activator is missing (%2$s). Reinstall the module ZIP from the latest release.
The %1$s module installation is corrupted: its activator is not executable (%2$s). Reinstall the module ZIP from the latest release.

The KPM module installation is corrupted: its activator is missing (%1$s). Install the complete vpnhide-kpm.zip as an APM/Magisk-compatible module through your root manager’s Modules screen; do not extract or load the inner vpnhide.kpm file by itself.

The KPM module installation is corrupted: its activator is not executable (%1$s). Install the complete vpnhide-kpm.zip as an APM/Magisk-compatible module through your root manager’s Modules screen; do not extract or load the inner vpnhide.kpm file by itself.
KPM is installed but cannot load on kernel %1$s because this kernel family has no validated offset table. Use the Zygisk backend instead.

Invalid KPM installation detected: KernelPatch loaded the standalone vpnhide.kpm file, but the vpnhide-kpm.zip module is not installed. The .kpm file alone has no VPN Hide activator, boot scripts, or configuration delivery, so protection will not work correctly. Remove or unload the standalone “vpnhide” entry in APatch/KPatch-Next (if it was embedded, repatch the boot image without it), install the complete vpnhide-kpm.zip from the Modules screen, then reboot.

KPM is installed and the KernelPatch runtime answered, but it refused the module control call — VPN Hide has no SuperKey saved, so it could only authenticate with the trusted su token. Save your SuperKey in Settings → Security (the same one you set in APatch/FolkPatch) and tap Refresh. Reinstalling the zip does not help.

KPM is installed, but the kernel is not patched with a KernelPatch runtime to load it. Install the KPatch-Next-Module and patch your kernel from its interface (it works on both Magisk and KernelSU). If that does not work, use APatch or FolkPatch instead.

The native backend loaded, but only %1$d of %2$d kernel hooks installed on this kernel — it could not resolve: %3$s. The detection surfaces behind them stay visible; everything else is still hidden. Reinstalling does not help: the functions are named differently (or absent) in this kernel build.
KPM installed but failed to load: %1$s. Use Settings → Debugging → Collect debug log to attach the full boot-time output to a bug report, or reinstall vpnhide-kpm.zip from the latest release.

More than one native backend is installed. Only one can be active at a time (priority: kernel module, then KPM, then Zygisk); the others sit idle. Uninstall the ones you don\'t use to keep things clean.
Debug logging is enabled. VPN Hide is writing verbose lines to logcat that anyone with root can read. Turn it off in Settings → Debugging after you\'ve finished collecting a bug report.
Agent control is enabled. VPN Hide is running a local debug bridge whose open port lets other apps on this device detect VPN Hide. Turn it off in Settings → Developer when you\'re done.

SELinux is Permissive. Six detection vectors VPN Hide relies on the kernel to block (RTM_GETROUTE, /proc/net/{tcp,udp,dev,fib_trie}, /sys/class/net) are reachable to selected apps. Run `setenforce 1` and investigate what disabled it.

VPN Hide is installed in %1$d profiles. The main-profile copy is the one that matters — LSPosed hooks system_server, which runs in the main profile only, and the picker there already sees apps from every profile and applies filters to all of them. Extra copies in secondary profiles are redundant and race each other\'s Saves to the shared config. Uninstall from work profile / Second Space / other secondary profiles.
No Native backend installed. Install the recommended Native backend for full hiding.
LSPosed/Vector is not installed. Install it and enable the VPN Hide module for System Framework.
LSPosed is configured correctly, but its hooks are not active yet. Reboot the device to activate them.
Failed to read LSPosed/Vector configuration. Reopen LSPosed/Vector, verify that VPN Hide is enabled there, and then reopen VPN Hide.
VPN Hide is present in LSPosed/Vector, but the module is disabled. Enable VPN Hide in LSPosed/Vector and keep System Framework in its scope.
VPN Hide is enabled in LSPosed/Vector, but System Framework is missing from its scope. Add System Framework to the VPN Hide scope in LSPosed/Vector.
VPN Hide should stay scoped only to System Framework in LSPosed/Vector. Remove these apps from the VPN Hide scope: %1$s. Use the Hiding tab in VPN Hide for filtering instead.

AOSP field rename detected on Android SDK %2$s: %1$s. Java-layer hiding is degraded for the affected hooks (they were skipped at install time to avoid logcat-spam from per-call NoSuchFieldError). Please file an issue at github.com/okhsunrog/vpnhide/issues with this list so the hooks can be updated for your Android version.
LSPosed/Vector reported hook install failures: %1$s. Collect a debug log and attach it to the issue so the failed hook can be fixed.
No target apps configured. Open Hiding and choose the apps you need.
Ports hiding module is installed, but no apps have Ports enabled. Open Hiding and enable Ports for the apps you need.
Ports is enabled for apps, but iptables rules are not active. Reboot or tap Save in Hiding; if it stays this way, collect a debug log so Ports load_status/load_log are included.
Ports is enabled for apps, but iptables rules are not active. Last apply failed: %1$s. Collect a debug log so Ports load_status/load_log are included.

Wrong kernel module variant: installed %1$s, your kernel needs %2$s. Uninstall the current kmod and install %3$s from the latest release.
Kernel module is installed but not loading, and the zip doesn\'t identify which GKI variant it was built for. Reinstall %1$s from the latest release to make sure it matches your kernel.
Kernel module %1$s failed to load this boot. Your kernel\'s GKI branch isn\'t identifiable from uname -r, so install %2$s instead.
Kernel module failed to load. insmod error: %1$s. Use Settings → Debugging → Collect debug log to attach the full boot-time insmod output to a bug report.

Your kernel enforces module signature verification, so the unsigned kernel module can\'t load (insmod failed with EKEYREJECTED — \"Key was rejected by service\"). Magisk can\'t disable this. Switch to KernelSU Next in GKI mode — it removes the enforcement and the kmod loads. On GKI kernels the kernel module is the right tool; don\'t fall back to Zygisk, whose in-process hooks are easily detected by banking and anti-fraud apps.
Your kernel (%1$s) has no matching vpnhide-kmod variant. Uninstall the kmod module and install %2$s instead.
Your kernel was built without CONFIG_KRETPROBES. The VPN Hide kernel module cannot work on this kernel. Uninstall kmod and use vpnhide-zygisk.zip instead.
Version %1$s is available. Tap to download.

Experimental: kernel backends intercept global VFS paths, while Zygisk provides best-effort libc filtering inside selected apps. No known real-world apps currently rely on this detection vector; standard Native protection should normally be sufficient.
Requires a kmod, KPM, or Zygisk native backend.
Off — standard Native protection is recommended.

These global VFS hooks may slow filesystem operations and are not currently needed for known real-world apps. Ordinary Native protection should normally be sufficient. Enable them only for explicit filesystem-path detection testing; a reboot is required.

Zygisk will add best-effort libc filesystem hooks inside selected apps. Raw syscalls and path aliases can bypass them. Enable this only for explicit filesystem-path detection testing; selected apps must be restarted.
